title: Cryptographic anchoring for usage events and subpoena readiness
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a tamper-evident, queryable evidence package for every billable usage event by cryptographically anchoring sequences of usage events and exposing a subpoena-ready proof API. The goal is to close gaps identified in recent audit drills where auditors and legal requested: (a) an indisputable timeline of events; (b) compact verifiable proof for a subset of events; and (c) controlled access to proofs for legal/finance. Deliverables include a signing/anchoring design, an archival policy (Object Lock + WORM), an API to retrieve signed proofs for event IDs or time ranges, and an operations runbook for legal requests and chain-of-custody reporting.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved that specifies per-event or per-batch cryptographic proofs (Merkle tree or chained hashes) and KMS/HSM signing strategy
Prototype pipeline produces cryptographic proofs for a synthetic workload and stores proofs in append-only storage with retention and immutability settings
Proof retrieval API returns a compact proof bundle (event record, proof path, signed root) and automated verification test that validates the bundle
RBAC and audit controls implemented for proof retrieval endpoints; access events are logged to the compliance audit stream
Runbook for legal/subpoena requests drafted and validated in a tabletop exercise; required artifacts are retrievable within SLA
Documentation and a SOC evidence package (artifact list + sample proof bundles) added to Confluence and attached to the release
implementation_steps: Design: evaluate per-event vs batched Merkle construction and choose canonical canonicalization format for usage events
Key management: define KMS asymmetric key usage policy, key rotation cadence, and HSM signing flow (Cloud KMS + customer-managed option)
Storage: configure append-only buckets with Object Lock and versioning; store raw events separately from proofs
Pipeline: implement a lightweight proof generator service that consumes billing events, computes tree roots, signs roots, and emits signed proof blobs
API: add /proofs endpoints to billing admin API that return proof bundles and a verification helper; instrument RBAC and audit logs
Retention & TTL: enforce retention windows tied to contract terms and legal hold flags; surface retention metadata in proof bundles
Testing: create integration tests that intentionally modify stored events to demonstrate tamper detection and monitor alerts
Operations: create legal response runbook with checklist, ticket template, and sample evidence packages for common request types
Telemetry: add metrics for proof generation latency, proof retrieval latency, archive integrity checks, and unauthorized access attempts

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Proof storage cost growth if we store full event copies with every proof. Mitigation: store compact canonicalized records and separate raw event archive with deduplication policy.
Risk: KMS signing throughput could become bottleneck. Mitigation: sign periodic roots rather than per-token, support local ephemeral signing in Dedicated clusters with later re-anchoring.
Risk: Legal requests may demand longer retention than standard contracts. Mitigation: support legal-hold flag to extend retention and surface hold in retention metadata.
Risk: Customers running Private deployments may require customer-managed keys. Mitigation: design option for customer HSM/KMS integration and include instructions in deployment docs.
